name: Reverse Pec Deck
description: The reverse pec deck uses the pec deck or butterfly machine in reverse — facing the pad rather than away from it — to perform a rear deltoid fly motion. The machine provides a guided movement path and consistent resistance throughout the arc, making it an effective and low-skill option for targeting the posterior deltoid and scapular retractors. It is widely used in hypertrophy programs as a finishing or high-rep accessory exercise for rear deltoid development.

execution.starting_position: Face the pec deck machine (reverse of the normal setup). Grip the handles with arms in front of the body at shoulder height. Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
execution.setup_instructions: Some pec deck machines have specific attachments or handle adjustments for reverse use. Position the seat so the arms are parallel to the floor at the start.
steps: Step 1: Face the machine, grip the handles with arms extended forward.
Step 2: Begin from the arms-forward position (handles together or close).
Step 3: Pull the handles outward and backward in a horizontal arc.
Step 4: Bring the arms to fully in line with the shoulders (T-position).
Step 5: Squeeze the rear delts and return under control.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the opening (fly) motion, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Letting the shoulder blades slide forward on the return — maintain upper back position
Using too heavy a load, causing the traps to dominate instead of the rear delts
safety_considerations: Keep the neck neutral — do not crane forward toward the machine
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arms start forward (closed position) and open to T (arms in line with shoulders).
coaching_cues: Think rear delt squeeze, not elbow drive
Slow and controlled on the return
